claims.text: The target material is single-phase, defect-free HfNbTaTiZr produced by spark plasma sintering of gas-atomized powder.
The target sample has low oxygen contamination of approximately 0.12 wt.%.
Second- and third-order force constants combined with an iterative phonon BTE can be used to calculate the lattice thermal conductivity.
The cited lattice-transport calculation uses the proposed second- and third-order force-constant iterative-BTE method.
KKR-CPA based on DFT electronic structure can separately compute the electronic thermal conductivity.
KKR-CPA provides a first-principles, configurationally averaged description of chemically disordered alloys within a single-site mean-field approximation.
Separately calculating lattice and electronic transport avoids conflating the two thermal-transport channels.
Second- and third-order force constants capture the relevant anharmonic phonon scattering in disordered HfNbTaTiZr.
Increasing temperature above 300 K increases anharmonic scattering and causes the lattice thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr to decline steeply.
The electronic thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr remains nearly temperature invariant from 300 K to 1200 K.
The predicted total thermal conductivity will agree with experiment within ±5%.
Earlier analytical and semi-empirical approaches typically agreed with experimental total thermal conductivity only within ±15%.
Achieving ±5% agreement would significantly outperform the earlier ±15% estimates.
Below 200 K, independently separated lattice and electronic contributions should be experimentally observable and consistent with prior experimental decoupling.
The model is applicable to defect-free, low-oxygen, spark-plasma-sintered HfNbTaTiZr from 300 K to 1200 K.
High oxygen content, grain boundaries, and other defects may introduce extrinsic scattering outside the model's applicability.
Magnetic fluctuations below 200 K may significantly alter phonon scattering.
Chemical disorder and anharmonic interactions present modeling challenges for the proposed framework.
The hypothesis is falsified if measured total thermal conductivity differs from the prediction by more than ±5%, or if the predicted channel-specific temperature trends are absent.

contradictions.description: The stated applicability and proposed measurements cover 300–1200 K, but the predicted outcome also makes a below-200 K claim. The proposed experiment therefore cannot test that low-temperature claim.
